forcedChoices.reason: Spanish 'realización' reads as 'accomplishment'; the section concerns how God is understood (science, religion, philosophy), so 'comprensión' fits the context best.
The quote addresses the Lord directly as one person in prayer; 'tú' is the natural form of address to God in Spanish prayer.

forcedChoices.choice: celo por el hombre / celos de él
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish separates zeal on behalf of someone (celo por) from envy of someone (celos de), which carries the English contrast 'jealous for' versus 'jealous of'.
Spanish 'su fe' could be read as the faith of the one who lives in me; the quote speaks to the readers, so the plural 'ustedes' is the clearest reading.
English 'must be' here is an inference, not an obligation; 'deber de' marks the inference in Spanish (also 4:1.10).
